first_week.eligible_universe: all Mondays from 2024-01-01 through 2025-11-24 excluding previously used candidate-02 weeks
first_week.selection_method: Python random.Random(seed).choice over chronologically sorted eligible Mondays

locked_hypothesis.event_detector: turnover-qualified one-boundary sweep of a frozen preceding eight-hour high or low
locked_hypothesis.local_reversion: the perpetual closes back inside, opposite displacement breaks internal structure, and the FVG retrace targets the nearest intact internal pivot rather than the opposite range boundary
locked_hypothesis.common_breakout_continuation: perpetual and spot both accept beyond the boundary without excessive basis expansion, breakout displacement leaves an FVG, and its retest holds outside before targeting the nearest intact external pivot
locked_hypothesis.ambiguous_state: no trade when final range acceptance and cross-market state do not identify exactly one scenario
locked_hypothesis.target_rule: nearest pre-existing confirmed and structurally intact five-minute pivot whose cost-after reward/risk is at least 1.10
locked_hypothesis.invalidation: beyond the sweep extreme for local reversion; accepted return inside the old range for continuation

promotion_rule: The central portfolio and at least one adjacent horizon must pass every original weekly gate, signals must span at least two UTC cycles, and no active state component may have negative after-cost expectancy. Otherwise run one core-variable ablation on the revealed week before discarding.

research_basis.reference: Osler, Stop-Loss Orders and Price Cascades in Currency Markets
research_basis.implication: a boundary break can be a noninformative positive-feedback cascade, so the sweep itself cannot determine direction

research_basis.reference: Cont, Kukanov and Stoikov, The Price Impact of Order Book Events
research_basis.implication: short-horizon price impact is tied to order-flow imbalance relative to depth rather than trade volume alone

research_basis.reference: Xu et al., Limit-order book resiliency after effective market orders
research_basis.implication: liquidity shocks can show either price resilience or continuation depending on event aggressiveness and replenishment

research_basis.reference: Hansen, Kim and Kimbrough, Periodicity in Cryptocurrency Volatility and Liquidity
research_basis.implication: fixed UTC dealing cycles are prospectively defensible because crypto liquidity and volatility have recurrent intraday patterns
